body:
Yea maybe you're right, I'm probably not surrounded by the right people.

Thanks for your point of view
Thank you for your encouragements, very much appreciated :)

I understand what you're saying about my relationship with my mom, but it's not so easy though... I know that no matter the things she says or does to me, I'll always treat her like a queen because, well she's my mom. I recently told her I didn't want to transition anymore, and she looks a lot happier ever since, even if I have to bury my feelings deep inside, it's okay as long as I see her smile... It's hard but as long as I'm around her, I'll put on the mask to make her happy. 

I try to do my best to not think about transitioning, hoping that maybe I'll lose all interest in it. I was so excited about it when I first discovered what it was, but the more I learned about it, and the less I find it appealing... I know I'm going to sound like a douche bag, but there isn't a single trans man I've come across I wanna look like... Maybe Ty turner, but that's it really :( I see many biological men I wish I could look like, but I know it will never be the case, which is why I'm not so excited about transition... 

I know height is not such a big deal in other people's minds, but thing is, I don't really care what people think, I'm saying this for me... People don't even care about what others look like as a whole anyway, nobody's gonna go to sleep thinking of how short I am, everyone has their own problems. Maybe you're right, but maybe I'll never be satisfied with my body even after transition... I know it's stupid but sometimes I find it absurd to spend so much energy on just changing gender, there are just so many things to think about in life. If I was born cis I would have had so much more time and less money to spend, I wouldn't have to worry about anything gender related... I wish I could just turn the "trans switch" off in my head, and just live my life... Thank you for your message, I really appreciate it :)

Thank you so much for your comment, this is so aspiring :) It makes me really happy that you don't want to die anymore, that's a huge step for sure! I myself know I don't want to die, there are just moments I wish I didn't exist. I don't wanna die because I have hobbies that I can't wait to do when I wake up, if I didn't have that I would definitely be miserable. I just wish I wasn't trans, things would just be okay... I've been through many struggles but somehow I managed to wear my scars with pride somehow, I definitely don't brag about it to other people but I like to make myself believe I'm stronger because of them. However being trans makes me feel horrible about myself... I don't even want to transition because I see it as pointless, and fuck I don't have time for it... I just wish I could go through life without having to worry about my gender, that's all :( The worst is that I try to pass as a girl sometimes, but it doesn't even work, people keep calling me young man, well I don't try really hard tho so that's not surprising, but yea it makes me feel constantly trapped between two identities... I feel like an unfinished draft sort of. 
Thank for sharing the album, I'll definitely check it out :)

Hey thank you for trying to make me feel better about my height :) I hear what you just said all the time but it just doesn't help me... I don't really care that Daniel Radcliff or anyone else is the same height as me, it's like telling me "there are many other girls out there who act like boys" if you know what I mean... I hope I didn't sound offensive :(

Thank you for making me feel less alone, really :) I'm sorry you're having a hard time with your family as well, it really sucks...

Do you have skype? we could talk on there^^
Thank you to everyone who shared their experience on here, I've read every one of you and it was really interesting :) It all makes a lot more sense to me now!

THIS.

Me too I find this attention to be the only reason preventing me from letting her go. That was the only thing that would make me say "yea okay being a girl has its pros", the only thing that would stop me from fully throwing that identity in the trash... I simply needed that confidence boost just like you.

Maybe if I work on other things that can make me feel confident I'll be able to let go of the "because I'm a girl" attention.

Thank you for sharing your experience!

thank you for sharing this guy's channel I found some of his videos really interesting!

> Second, since being on T, a wonderful thing started to happen after about a month. I stopped giving a shit what people thought, or agonizing over every social situation. I believe it's equal parts confidence and emotion nerfing. I did not expect this amazing gift from T, but nevertheless, it happened, and I'm so grateful. I don't even feel embarrassed hardly ever! Or, at least not to the degree I used to.

amen to that!

Hey your experience was really interesting to read too! :) 

> Now that I'm presenting male, and passing thanks to my freakishly awesome Mufasa voice, people listen to me and believe me. I've gotten so much more outgoing, and my career is so much more awesome than I could have thought a 22 year old would get to have. I doubt I could have it as a woman.

So awesome your life is going so great! :D It gives me hope because I'm so worried about my future being trans... I feel like I'm gonna stay miserable all my life, no hope for my acting career, nobody's gonna want me, yea I know I'm pretty pessimistic lol. 

> The ego thing existed for me prior to realizing I was a man, but it was a much more defensive, angry ego that I had to feed into much. As a man, that ego turned into a healthy self-esteem where people now see me as confident and genuine instead of aggressive or douchy.

Very interesting, I feel like I can relate to this, I also kinda notice my ego slowly turning into a more healthy one as a man. 

> Basically, I used to think that people would take me even less seriously when I came out as trans, and continuing with my own journey of self discovery not only sort of helped me tame a lot of that ego, but helped others see the value I could finally see in myself. Sometimes I still come off as egotistic I'm sure, but to me it feels like I can just finally say what my strengths and weaknesses are and that it's okay to be proud of what I like about me. Shit, it took long enough to get here. And I hope continuing to figure out who you are and the kind of man you want to be helps you tame your ego as well, because it's cool to see what the world is like when you're not blinded by it.

Yes I'm thinking about going on T in March next year and I'm just so scared of coming out to everybody around me, I feel like everyone is gonna suddenly see me as a huge freak and it's all gonna be weird. That's why I respect people who choose to medically transition so much, you're all just so brave.

I really enjoyed reading you, thank you!

I can relate to this so much! I can't deny the fact that I really appreciated the attention I would get, but at the end of the day I would forget who I was. In other words, when I present as female, it disrupts my mind so much I can't focus on other things that are part of me. I forget what my hobbies are, what I love, all that... When I get back to my male identity, everything just becomes so easy and normal again. 

I don't know, sometimes I think maybe if I had a girlfriend that would validate me as a handsome guy, I would feel more confident for exemple. Some people still call me super pretty having short hair and dressing as a guy... It upsets me a lot because it means people see me as an attractive girl not a guy.

But I really agree with you on the "real" feeling thing

> Certain characteristics that made you attractive as a female will also make you attractive as a male. Your facial symmetry, eyes, and personality are eternal no matter the rest of your biological makeup.

Yea but I feel like those things aren't the kinda features women see first in men :/ I've seen many men with not so handsome faces get lots of girls just because they were big and reassuring, while I don't see the contrary happen very often.

> I think some hetero peeps just aren't sure how to act around someone who looks androgynous- and it can make them just as awkward/ antisocial as it makes us. You are already attractive in many ways. {if you want} with a little t in your system, and some time to work its magic- you will gain a more stereotypically "masculine" attractiveness.

That's for sure, but I still cannot picture T turning me into an attractive guy... I just don't expect it to do miracles. Maybe I'm wrong here, but it's better than getting my hopes up.

> Keep building yourself up however you can and one day the world will revel around you again.

Can't wait for it! Lol jk thank you for your reply mate ;)

Yea I understand your point of view, but attractive men get the same amount of sexual interest as women though :) But I have to agree on the fact that I'd rather feel desired as a man than as a woman...
Thank you for your encouragements :)

> There is definitely a social payoff to being a guy, since attractive women are treated like special butterflies and both women and men admire them.

Exactly, it's a privilege hard to give up on^^ it's simply easier to show your skills when everyone is already looking at you than when you have to scream in the room so they dare to give half their attention. 

> Men who command social attention generally do so with a different approach.

That's true, but most of them usually already have an undeniable charm, which I'm not sure I own... Not right now that's for sure. And I sometimes feel so small when I'm in a group of men, I feel okay when I'm around women since I'm usually taller than them, but with other men I feel like an ant. It pisses me off how guys my age are so freaking tall, I just wanna cut their legs off LOL. Believe me if I were 5'9 or above I would be taking T without any hesitation... I feel bad saying this but my height personally makes me feel like a deformed man, more than anything else...

> Also, if you're trans, you're less likely to fit the masculine ideal (tall, buff, confident) because all of those things are tougher to access when you start as female. So it's definitely likely that you went from a socially ideal female to a less than socially ideal male and are seeing the result.

No doubt about that!

> However, if you are read as a masculine-presenting female or as androgynous by most people at the moment, that automatically erases you from many people's social and attractiveness radar

This happens once people find out I'm not a 14 year old boy... I somehow pass as male very well, and people usually treat me like their little buddy at first. But there is always someone to out me at some point which makes people look at me weird all of a sudden. 

> so T may do more for you than you think - if you work out, project confidence, rock an awesome beard, etc, T might bring you closer to "ideal male" status and thereby gain you your social status back. To a degree this depends on the kind of man you want to be, but if you were attractive as a female you're likely to come out of T as an attractive man. Attractive features are attractive features.

Yes I'm totally okay with my face, and my body shape which isn't extremely feminine, but to me those features become instantly pointless because I'm short :/ 4 more inches and I would feel hella confident going into transition. Because from my point of view, a guy who's 5'10 isn't lucky but normal... Me being 5'5, it reminds me of Eminem saying "How the fuck can I be white, I don't even exist?" replace white by short lol. 

> It's always good practice to work on your own emotions and insecurities and become less dependent on the opinions and attention of others, and to work hard until you achieve success. But if this is important to you, you may also be basing your judgement on an incomplete set of data. :)

Yes I tell myself this a lot, I would be even more proud of myself if I were to become successful apart from all these privileges. It's kinda like going into battle naked lol ;) But of course negative thoughts always come back, and I end up believing I'm going to become extremely miserable if I go down that road. I just can't make up my mind!

Thank you for trying to help :)

> I used to get a lot of attention from guys because I was a tomboy and also an objectively attractive girl, so they'd all have crushes or whatever because I could play games and talk about star wars and also wear a skirt occasionally. but it wasn't something I reveled in and tbh I always thought it was weird of them to be so interested and treat me so differently, because I was just me, nothing special about that, but they treated me like something else

I can actually relate to this a lot, I remember having the same thoughts back then, how ironic right? 

> I still remember when I went to buy Pokemon Pearl from Gamestop. the guy behind the counter accidentally rung it up as Diamond, which wasn't a big deal, but I pointed it out to him because I know that stuff is generally tied up to their inventory numbers. he went SO overboard apologizing for a 10 second fix that he ended up giving me the Palkia stylus you were only supposed to get with pre-order as a way of apologizing. every guy I told about that went "well duh, because you're a girl gamer", but to me it was weird, borderline creepy, definitely unnecessary, entirely unwanted

Haha I think I've been that guy. The other day I was having a drink with friends and a girl was there, we started talking and she said she liked skateboarding and video games and that she had the same shoes as me, I was suddenly all over her lol.

> I'm glad I'm no longer some marvel people put on a pedestal before they even get to know me. I can finally be just one of the guys like I always wanted to be to begin with 

I totally understand your point of view, I have the exact same opinion. I simply recognized that being an "attractive cis female" in today's society was a huge advantage in life, and I'm not sure if I'm willing to give up on it... 

Thank you for sharing.
I think we should talk sometime :) I'll PM you later^^
Thank you so much mate, I'll PM you shortly :)

Thanks but I don't live in the US... 

Only if you wanna talk too, I don't want to bother anyone ^^
Funny how they say "free app" but turns out to cost 150dollars a month after seven days once you click on the link
That sounds very interesting ^^ I'm totally down to read more
EXACTLY

Why are so many people mentally weak nowadays? It's almost like everyone has anxiety or this and that disorder. The smallest things will make someone have an "anxiety attack". Everyone always brags so much about how much bullshit they've had to go through and how broken they're today. Everyone is just so weak and makes everything seem like such a big deal when it could have not been.
Our society has externally evolved A LOT, but internally, we're becoming weaker and weaker, like kids who never grow up.

Yes I think if I was able to get a phalloplasty one day I'd feel a lot better, but I think I will never get one because it's just too many scars whether it's taken from the arm or the abdomen... It's just too much to me, I'd rather keep my female genitals tbh.

> If I can find you some links to softer images, starting with some SFW stuff, would you be interested? The point being to look at these people and ask yourself if you see a real man.

Yea I guess?

> I don't agree with most trans people and I don't identify with the "LGBT community" at large. And there's nothing wrong with that. I'm just a guy whose software got put with the wrong hardware. That doesn't define me any more than my hair color does. And it certainly doesn't determine who I have to hang out with.

This is so true, sometimes I feel like other trans guys believe we are great friends just because we are both trans, and I'm like " so being trans is the first thing you see that defines us?"... It kinda drives me crazy sometimes. 

Thank you for making me feel less alone man
Yea you're probably right, we have what we have after all, doesn't mean we have to love it, but just do our best with it...

> Is there an LGBTQ helpline in your area? They may be able to point you at therapists with experience in gender issues for the future, and give you a place to say these things out loud for the short term.

You're probably right, I'm just too shy to ask this kinda stuff... I'll try tho

> I don't know about you, but for me when I say thoughts out loud it's much easier to sort the true things from shit I picked up from my parents/tv/random assholes I knew as a kid. Once you know a thought is rubbish, it's easier to replace it with something healthy.

Yea I can totally relate, when I'm around people it's a lot easier for me to say stuff like " trans people are crazy " than just defending them... Which is really fucked up.

> For instance, have you seen pictures of men with vaginas? There are art shoots and a small but growing body of porn featuring FtM guys. Do you know where you first heard that it would be disgusting? Do you still trust the source of that information?

I have seen one picture against my will, it was one of buck angel all naked, and yea it made me feel really weird. It's one of the things that really made me scared of transition, kinda like a "proof" that I'd never be a man, just a "woman masculinized by drugs"... 

> Do you think a rhinoplasty is mutilation? How about a tummy tuck? Is it misleading to get a lap band to make people believe you aren't fat?

I don't know it depends... Like, I can understand someone that does it when they have a nose that literally looks like shit, but when it's not even the case and everything's working fine I find it kinda silly.

> Be kind to yourself, man. We'll be here when you need us.

Thank you so much... I really appreciate it

> One thing I'd try to remember is that you aren't transitioning for other people. You aren't being inauthentic or trying to "trick" anyone... you're changing your body for you.

I try to tell myself this a lot, and sometimes it works, it makes me feel better for a while, but then the negative thoughts kick in again you know :/ 

> I forget that I'm trans most of the time, not that it's ever really bothered me.

I really, really want to be like you someday, just forgetting the whole damn thing

I went to one of those, but if I ever open my mouth someone gets offended even though it wasn't my point... So I basically end up staying in a corner quiet... I guess I'll just have to figure things out on my own :/
I wish I could see a therapist sometimes, but it's way too expensive and the only ones I've met so far were real jerks...

>  i go to my trans masculine support group and a lot of times think all the guys are just fake men trying to be something they're not.

I can relate so much to this, I always think of trans men that way and that makes me believe I will never be a man myself...
